operator.description: Atomically resolve all independent intents in an owned request with expectedRevision CAS. Creates visible pinned tasks without workers; followUp links concrete task IDs. Questions/status/ack use none or question; corrections use update and existing taskId. Retry the same intent keys; conflicts return current state. A single pasted PR URL is attached to a single work task atomically. Ambiguous URLs require explicit references mapping; use generic named references for unknown providers. Preserve existing PR unless replacement was explicitly requested. No execution/publish authority is granted.

compact.description: omit pinned template bodies from returned tasks; evidence and policy remain

expectedRevision.description: current host request revision for atomic resolution

intents.description: 1-8 independent actions with stable key, kind(create/followUp/update/question/none/untracked), reason; create/followUp adds cwd, title, provenance(explicit/inferred), optional workflowId(null=no workflow, id=chosen policy, omitted=default); untracked records an explicit opt-out with key/kind/reason only and creates no task; update requires taskId and expectedTaskRevision; workflowId may change only before the first worker; followUp requires dependsOn task IDs or dependsOnKeys naming earlier work intents in this same resolution; cancel is optional on update; references optionally maps pasted URLs using kind pullRequest(number,url), ticket(id,url), or reference(label,url); multiple URLs/tasks require references on every work intent ([] assigns none); replacePullRequest true requires explicit replacement intent

requestId.description: host request ID returned by list_manager_requests; never derive from chat text

operator.name: resolve_manager_request

operator.description: Redispatch a worker: clone a session's ORIGINAL task and cwd/model/provider/parent/role, append your correction, and start a fresh agent with both. The standing move for a worker that has crept out of scope — stop it (signal SIGTERM, then close_session), then respawn_with the diagnosis baked in, instead of re-authoring the whole first message by hand. Returns the new sessionId.

amendment.description: the correction, in your words: what went wrong and what the successor must do differently. It is appended to the original task under a clear heading, so state the DIAGNOSIS, not the whole task again

capability.description: override the model CAPABILITY the successor is dispatched at (cheap | balanced | frontier | frontier_max | reviewer | deep_reviewer | frontier_plus); defaults to the original's. Copy it from a fresh select_model answer rather than raising it by hand — the host still clamps it to the target directory's ceiling

contextWindow.description: canonical context-window override in tokens; pair with modelIdentity

cwd.description: override the working directory; defaults to the original's — which for a ship task is its WORKTREE, so the successor continues on the same branch with the partial work in place. Pass the repo path (with worktree:true) to start clean instead

effort.description: override the reasoning effort; defaults to the original's

hub.description: the peer hub this session lives on — the hub field on its list_agents row; omit for a local session

label.description: label for the successor; defaults to the original's with a retry marker

model.description: override the model (e.g. step up for a task that proved harder than it looked); defaults to the original's

modelIdentity.description: canonical provider model identity override; pair with contextWindow. The legacy model companion is derived for old peers

role.description: override the work ROLE the successor is dispatched as (scout | implementer | reviewer | deep_reviewer | fixer | complex_fixer | validator | diagnostician | mechanical | judge); defaults to the original's. Set it when the redispatch changes what the worker IS — a failed implementer respawned to diagnose is a diagnostician, not an implementer

sessionId.description: the session to clone — usually one you have just stopped

toolScope.description: accepted and ignored compatibility field; supported successors receive the full Workspacer tool surface automatically

trackTask.description: false to keep an explicitly untracked retry out of task history; parent/wakes remain

worktree.description: carve a FRESH isolated worktree for the successor instead of reusing the original's cwd; use when the partial work should be abandoned rather than continued

operator.name: respawn_with

operator.description: Read this connected hub's safe routing defaults, managed preferences, source revision and cached catalog.
operator.name: routing_preferences_get

operator.description: Clear managed routing preferences to inherited host/shipped values; authenticated host authority and current baseRevision required.
operator.name: routing_preferences_reset

operator.description: Atomically apply a validated routing patch on this hub; authenticated host authority and current baseRevision required.
operator.name: routing_preferences_save

operator.description: Validate a sparse typed routing patch against its source revision without writing; authenticated host authority required.
operator.name: routing_preferences_validate

operator.description: Preview a route and reasons without spawning, audit rows or decision events; uses bounded cached provider state.

account.description: the account key the spawn will bill to; omit for the provider's default login

cwd.description: the project directory the work happens in — it selects which per-directory routing ceiling applies

decisionDensity.description: low | medium | high — how many consequential decisions are NOT already made for the agent. A 1500-line mechanical migration is low; a 20-line authorization change is high

expectedWork.description: the work still AHEAD before the window resets, as counts per workflow phase — e.g. [{phase: implementation, count: 2}, {phase: review, count: 4}]. Weighted by the matrix's forecast_weights and REPORTED with its arithmetic on the answer (demand.units / demand.phases); it does not become a percentage, so on its own it leaves demand UNKNOWN for the mode rules. Pass forecastDemandBeforeResetPct when you know the actual share — that wins over this

count.description: how many agent runs of that phase are still expected before the window resets

phase.description: the workflow phase, from the matrix's forecast_weights keys: scouting | implementation | review | fixing | validation. A phase the matrix has no weight for is REPORTED back as unweighted rather than counted as free

forecastDemandBeforeResetPct.description: how much of this provider's allowance you expect the work still ahead to consume before the window resets, as a percentage. 0 is a real answer meaning 'nothing more is coming' and is what unlocks spend-down; omitting it leaves demand UNKNOWN, which keeps routing in normal mode

previousProvider.description: the provider that ran the PREVIOUS agent on this work, so a reviewer can be given a different model family from the implementer

profile.description: a routing profile to resolve under (mixed | codex_only | anthropic_only); omit to use whichever the matrix has active

profileId.description: a Claude profile id, used as the account key when account is omitted

provider.description: ask about ONE provider (claude | codex | copilot | opencode | pi): the answer then reports that provider's capacity and refuses rather than silently substituting another one

Additive: the worker still writes its prose summary, and a missing or invalid block reports itself instead of failing the dispatch. A valid terminal wks-escalation is the one alternative: it gets its own wake card without a contradictory missing-result error. Desktop-only (the headless brain declines arbitrary resultSchema, while still providing its fixed escalation contract)

view.description: Tell the agent that dispatched you how your task is going, mid-task, in ONE line — a phase landed, the approach you were given is wrong, you are burning context faster than expected. It goes to your manager and nowhere else (you cannot name a recipient, and you have no way to reach any other session with it), it does NOT end your turn or your task, and your final message still reaches your manager in full when you finish. Limited to one per minute and 20 per session; use it when your manager's next decision would change, not to narrate.

needsDecision.description: true if you are BLOCKED on your manager's answer rather than just keeping it informed; it is marked NEEDS A DECISION. The channel is one-way either way — your manager replies (if it replies) with a message to you, so keep working if you can

note.description: ONE line, in your own words, about your own run — a phase that landed, an approach that is not working, a budget you are burning faster than expected. Not a report: say what changed for your manager's DECISION and leave the detail for your final message, which it receives in full. Max 500 characters

view.name: report_progress

view.description: On demand: summarize what a visible agent is doing from bounded task and recent text. Uses the source hub's configured CLI provider/model; requires a compatible desktop and daemon there. Availability status is not worker lifecycle. Never poll this tool or substitute it for direct blocked/completion evidence or the final worker report. Include hub from list_agents for remote sessions.

hub.description: the peer hub this session lives on — the hub field on its list_agents row; omit for a local session

sessionId.description: Session id from list_agents; include its hub for a remote session

view.name: summarize_agent_status
